prompt: Which signal answers 'where did the time go' across several services?

choices.text: Logs written by the load balancer for each connection it opens
choices.why: They record events at one point, not the path through every service.

choices.text: Health checks
choices.why: They say up or down.

choices.text: Traces
choices.why: Right. Lesson 8 builds them.

choices.text: Metrics, summed over every request of every service and every copy
choices.why: Sums say how much, not where one request spent its time.

prompt: Why are metrics cheap compared with logs?

choices.text: Prometheus is free and log systems are paid
choices.why: Both exist free; cost here is volume.

choices.text: Metrics are compressed and logs are not
choices.why: Both can be compressed; the count of records differs.

choices.text: A counter is one number however many requests it counts
choices.why: Right. Logs cost in proportion to traffic.

choices.text: Metrics are only kept for an hour
choices.why: Retention is a setting, not the reason.

prompt: What does RED stand for?

choices.text: Rate, errors, duration
choices.why: Right: the service from its users' side.

choices.text: Rate, errors, disk, for the resources a service runs on
choices.why: Resources are USE's subject.

choices.text: Requests, events, dashboards
choices.why: Not the list.

choices.text: Replicas, errors, databases
choices.why: Not the list.

prompt: In USE terms, what were the fifteen connections waiting on a Lock in lesson 1's hot row?

choices.text: Saturation
choices.why: Right: work waiting for a resource, here one row's lock.

choices.text: Rate, since fifteen requests were being handled at once by the database
choices.why: They were not being handled; they were waiting.

choices.text: Errors
choices.why: Every sale succeeded.

choices.text: Utilisation
choices.why: Utilisation is how busy the resource is, not how much waits.

prompt: tickets_requests_total is a counter. What happens to it when a copy restarts?

choices.text: It keeps its value on disk
choices.why: prometheus_client keeps metrics in memory.

choices.text: It goes negative until the copy catches up with the others
choices.why: Counters never go below zero.

choices.text: It starts again from zero
choices.why: Right, and rate() treats the fall as a reset.

choices.text: Prometheus restores it from the last scrape
choices.why: The copy's memory is gone; Prometheus only records.

prompt: Match each metric type to what its value means.

pairs.right: only grows; its rate is the information
goes up and down; its value now is the information

prompt: Why does observe() catch every exception and reply 500?

choices.text: A 500 is faster than a closed connection
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

choices.text: Otherwise the error is never counted or logged
choices.why: Right. An uncaught exception closes the connection and leaves nothing in the metrics.

choices.text: Python's server would otherwise stop
choices.why: It survives a handler's exception; the request is what is lost.

choices.text: nginx refuses to forward an exception
choices.why: nginx sees a closed connection, and answers 502.

prompt: Why does Prometheus scrape each copy directly instead of asking through nginx?

choices.text: Scraping through nginx is slower
choices.why: The problem is which copy answers, not speed.

choices.text: Through nginx it would get one copy's numbers, a different one each time
choices.why: Right. A counter needs every copy's own value.

choices.text: Prometheus cannot speak HTTP/1.1 keepalive
choices.why: It can; that is not the reason.

choices.text: nginx blocks /metrics
choices.why: The capture fetched /metrics through nginx.

prompt: Why does the lesson call up the first thing to alert on?

choices.text: A copy that stops being scraped silently leaves every graph
choices.why: Right. Its numbers disappear without anything looking wrong.

choices.text: It is the only metric that does not need labels to be read
choices.why: It has instance and job labels.

choices.text: It measures latency
choices.why: It is 1 or 0: scraped or not.

choices.text: It counts errors
choices.why: Errors are in tickets_requests_total.

prompt: Prometheus fetching a program's /metrics page is called a ___ .
What does rate(tickets_requests_total[30s]) return?

choices.text: The average latency of the last 30 seconds, per route and status
choices.why: Latency is in the histogram; this is a counter.

choices.text: The total since the copy started
choices.why: That is the raw counter.

choices.text: The requests of the last 30 s, one per line
choices.why: Metrics keep no individual requests.

choices.text: Per-second increase over 30 s
choices.why: Right.

prompt: The box office reported 338 sales a second and the load generator 331. What does the lesson make of that?

choices.text: The generator is wrong
choices.why: Both are right about different windows.

choices.text: Two independent measurements agree, so the instrumentation is right
choices.why: Right. The small gap is the window each one covered.

choices.text: Seven sales a second are being lost
choices.why: Every sale answered 201; the windows differ.

choices.text: Prometheus double-counts
choices.why: Then it would be near 660.

prompt: How many requests were in progress across the copies when sum(tickets_in_flight) was asked?
Why is a percentile computed from a histogram an estimate?

choices.text: It only knows which bucket the value falls in
choices.why: Right. Inside the bucket, it interpolates.

choices.text: Prometheus samples one request in a hundred
choices.why: Every request is counted.

choices.text: Latencies are rounded to the nearest millisecond before they are stored in each bucket
choices.why: Rounding is not the cause; bucket width is.

choices.text: Scrapes lose some requests
choices.why: Counters are cumulative; nothing is lost between scrapes.

prompt: Three copies each report their own p95. Why not average them for the box office's p95?

choices.text: Averages are not allowed in PromQL
choices.why: avg() exists; it gives the wrong answer here.

choices.text: One copy usually gets most of the slow requests
choices.why: Even with equal copies the average of percentiles is not a percentile.

choices.text: Percentiles do not combine; bucket counts do
choices.why: Right. sum by (le) first, then one quantile.

choices.text: The copies have different buckets
choices.why: They run the same code.

prompt: For reads, the histogram said 20 ms and the load generator 30 ms. What explains it?

choices.text: The generator is slower than the box office
choices.why: It measures; it does not add time to the server.

choices.text: The generator also timed nginx and the network
choices.why: Right. An inside latency is a lower bound on what users see.

choices.text: Prometheus scrapes delay requests
choices.why: A scrape is one small request every five seconds.

choices.text: The histogram's buckets are 10 ms wide
choices.why: Bucket width blurs; it does not shift by a third.

prompt: Of 1000 requests, 940 took up to 100 ms and 990 up to 250 ms. Interpolating evenly inside the bucket, what p95 does the histogram give, in ms?
hint: The 950th request is 10 of the 50 in the 100–250 bucket.

prompt: Why does the box office write each log line as one JSON object?

choices.text: Docker only accepts JSON
choices.why: Docker keeps any output.

choices.text: JSON is shorter than text
choices.why: It is usually longer.

choices.text: It encrypts the content of each line so that only the log system can read it
choices.why: JSON is plain text.

choices.text: So a program can search it by field
choices.why: Right. It arrives already taken apart.

prompt: With the replica stopped, what did the client see, and where was the real cause?

choices.text: A timeout; the cause was unknown
choices.why: The answer came at once.

choices.text: The full Python traceback; nothing was logged
choices.why: Clients get a short message on purpose.

choices.text: A short 500; the cause was in the error log line
choices.why: Right: AdminShutdown, for the server on the other end.

choices.text: A 502 from nginx; the cause was in nginx's log
choices.why: The try in observe turned it into a 500.

prompt: Which field does the lesson say must not go into a log line?

choices.text: The buyer's e-mail
choices.why: Right. Logs are copied widely and kept long.

choices.text: The name of the copy that answered, taken from the container's host name
choices.why: It is how a failure is traced to one copy.

choices.text: The route template
choices.why: That is exactly what a log line should carry.

choices.text: The duration in milliseconds
choices.why: Useful and harmless.

prompt: Why does the box office label requests with /events/{id} rather than the real path?

choices.text: Each path would be a separate series
choices.why: Right. Series multiply by every label's values.

choices.text: The real path would reveal what users buy to anyone who could read the metrics
choices.why: The lesson's reason is cost, not privacy.

choices.text: Prometheus refuses slashes in label values
choices.why: The template has slashes.

choices.text: Templates are faster to compare
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: A histogram with 11 buckets is labelled by route (4 values) and status (3 values) on 5 copies. How many bucket series is that?
Where does a value per user or per request belong, by the lesson?

choices.text: In the metric's name, so that each user gets a metric of their own
choices.why: Same explosion, by another route.

choices.text: In logs or traces
choices.why: Right: where unique details are expected.

choices.text: Nowhere; it should not be recorded
choices.why: It is useful, in the right signal.

choices.text: In a metric label
choices.why: That is the cardinality explosion.

prompt: Which is an SLO rather than an SLI?

choices.text: The fraction of sales answered within 250 ms
choices.why: That is the indicator, without a target.

choices.text: tickets_request_seconds_bucket
choices.why: A metric the SLI is built from.

choices.text: The sales that may fail
choices.why: That is the error budget.

choices.text: 99.9% of sales within 250 ms over 30 days
choices.why: Right: a target over a window.

prompt: An SLO of 99.5% over 30 days allows how many minutes of complete outage?
Which alert does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: Any error
choices.why: The budget exists to absorb some.

choices.text: The availability falling below 100% for one minute
choices.why: 100% is not a target worth having.

choices.text: The budget being spent fast enough to run out within hours
choices.why: Right. Worth waking up for.

choices.text: Any request slower than the objective
choices.why: A single slow request is noise.

prompt: At 03:10 sales got slow. Which order of signals does the lesson describe for finding out why?

choices.text: Only logs, read from 03:00 onwards until the slow sales appear
choices.why: That answers slowly; metrics narrow it down first.

choices.text: Trace, then log, then metric
choices.why: Without a metric you do not know which traces to look at.

choices.text: Log, then metric, then trace
choices.why: Logs are the detail, read last.

choices.text: Metric, then trace, then log
choices.why: Right: how much and when, then where, then what exactly.
